trails.title: Rational Passion
trails.description: Don't let the white coats and good manners fool you—those people are absolutely mad!

content.text: "No Longer Poles Apart" Research Project Proposal

Dear and wonderful Ms. Nautika, Laplace Scientific Computing Center has taken a keen interest in your new body. We are writing in hopes that you will agree to participate in our experiments and research. Rest assured, we remain fully committed to humanitarian care and professional research ethics—which is why you are welcome to check off only the projects you are willing to take part in. The research projects regarding "No Longer Poles Apart" are listed below:

√1. October 13 - December 20, Research Theme: Biotic Force Field and Arcane Cell Compatibility in "No Longer Poles Apart"
     Projects: Blood draw (a significant volume of blood samples is required—you are welcome to decline if you are sensitive to pain), lab analysis, Picrasma Candy sensitivity test, triathlon comparative study (humans as control group), epidermal cell stress test, unknown mucus DNA sequencing ...

√2. November 4 - January 29, Research Theme: Psychological Study of Self-Identity and Special Socialization Based on the Reconstructed Body of "No Longer Poles Apart"
     Theme: Social anxiety assessment in the tiered lecture hall, avoidance-attachment relationship test in the auditorium (you are welcome to share your mythological archaeology), physical coordination test in Uluru Stadium, emotional and psychological clinical evaluation ...

√3. December 15 - January 30, Research Theme: Spatial Compatibility of the Photon Dynamic Holographic Dress with "No Longer Poles Apart"
     Content: Human-form photon holographic dress design study, personal aesthetic preference research (we're very curious!), compatibility study of photon dress materials with mucus and bone, cell photosensitive spectrum determination range study, height measurement, weight measurement, arm—or wing—span measurement ...

items.text: Vacuum of Arcanum
Countdown to the "Storm"
Hallway, St. Pavlov Foundation

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Ah. They're not here either.
Regulus dispels her optical stealth with a frown.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: Captain, I find it rather unlikely that the leader of the Manus Orchestra would simply be hiding in a room waiting for us to wander into them.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: Assuming they have an orchestra at all and that there's someone leading it.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Fair point, Mr. APPLe, but I'm not letting any sensible conclusions hold me back. Not after all that clanging and clattering battered my poor ears on the "Free Breeze."

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Besides, my dear chief mate, why else would they have become all musical instrument-y if there weren't some barmy conductor leading it all?

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Therefore, ipso facto, Bob's your uncle, this conductor must be operating from behind enemy lines.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: And if I may ask, Captain, what will we do if we actually find this conductor?

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Simple. That's when we bust out the "Gluey Gooey Gum Gun" our dear old X sent us.

items.speaker: Manus Believer
items.text: ㄞ!

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Urgh, you tone-deaf twit. Listen, if you can't play a proper tune, then stop acting like an instrument. It's insulting!

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: Captain, I strongly advise we make a tactical retreat.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Not to worry, Mr. APPLe. It's only one measly Manus—

items.speaker: Taira
items.text: What's this? A Foundation fool has sneaked their way behind our lines.
Even more shadowy figures emerge behind the crab-faced warrior.

items.speaker: Taira
items.text: Seize her! And that apple as well.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Cor, look at that face. He's redder than the guy on the King Crimson album. Come on, Mr. APPLe. Let's give this Gum Gun a try.
Eyes up, soldier.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Huh?

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Whoaa!

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: Captain!
The explosion causes Regulus to stumble and coats APPLe's peel in dust.
Someone lands inside the dust, and after a quick survey confirms their enemies have been eliminated, she turns to Regulus.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Well, well. What are the chances?

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: L—*cough*—Lilya? You took your bloody time and a half, didn't you? They were saying the Flying Witches wouldn't make it.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Ha! Then "they" clearly don't know how fast my brand-new Red 38 flies or who they're talking about.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: So, what, we take our eyes off this place for ten minutes and the Manus are all over you? Look at all these Olitiaus buzzing like flies on a corpse. Makes my skin crawl.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Whatever, catch you later, rockstar. But don't forget. You owe me one. And I mean something harder than Dr. Papper.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: That's it? You just swoop in, save the day, and fly off? Why not stick around and give these Manus stooges a bit of what for?

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Oh, I will. But I'm not wasting my time charging around on foot.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Plenty of stooges to deal with outside the Committee Building. Spotted them taking out some heavy machinery on my way in. Things are about to get wild.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: You two should get moving. Let the Foundation know what's up. And no more wandering off. I don't babysit.
Lilya mounts her new broom and takes off into the sky again.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Wait! Is Dr. Papper really out of the question?
Vice President's Office
Madam Z watches Lilya's broom arc through the sky.

items.speaker: Z
items.text: We've gotten reports that the first group of Flying Witches has arrived. But I only see one of them, Lilya.

items.speaker: Constantine
items.text: She's the quickest of them, no doubt. But even her entire squad won't be enough to turn the tide.

items.speaker: Constantine
items.text: It's time, Z.

items.speaker: Z
items.text: But ma'am, withdrawing now could damage morale.

items.speaker: Constantine
items.text: I trust our soldiers. After all, we're not fighters. Our presence here does nothing but slow them down.

items.speaker: Constantine
items.text: Contact every Committee member and House of Integratus representative you can reach. We're relocating to the top floor of the Spire by the president's order.

items.speaker: Z
items.text: The Spire ... Understood. Is there anything you'd like me to bring, ma'am?

items.speaker: Constantine
items.text: Your kettle and some tea. You'll need it.

items.speaker: Z
items.text: You don't seem at all concerned. Is there something I don't know about?
Pyrodrake Phlogiston Incendiaries rain down on the Manus. Though few in number, they're enough to throw the enemy's reserves into a panic.
Southern Garden, St. Pavlov Foundation

items.speaker: Manus Soldier II
items.text: Cannon, the cannon!

items.speaker: Manus Soldier II
items.text: Damn it, cannon's lost! Get out of here! Those trees are catching fire!
The Manus soldiers scatter and flee the mazelike gardens. From the air, they look like startled ants.

items.speaker: Ritualist
items.text: Witches! How did they get here so quickly?
A dark-clad soldier crosses a hedge to reach the ritualist.

items.speaker: Manus Soldier I
items.text: Ma'am, General Krutov has sent word again.

items.speaker: Ritualist
items.text: Do I look like I have time for his sniveling? Tell him to fix his own messes.

items.speaker: Ritualist
items.text: I would have had the array ready for those Flying Witches if you idiots hadn't kept getting in my way.
The ritualist pushes the frightened soldier aside and walks toward a building near the garden.
Hallway, Southern Annex
Infuriated, she enters the building. The hall inside is oddly cool amid the fires of battle.

items.speaker: Ritualist
items.text: Buzz all you like, pests. I'll clip your wings soon enough. We need to move the array rites elsewhere.

items.speaker: Ritualist
items.text: Somewhere those irksome flies cannot bother us. Not under a roof, but nowhere fully exposed.

items.speaker: Ustrina
items.text: Was this not the place set aside for you?

items.speaker: Ritualist
items.text: You've got some nerve asking that. Where have you been? Off in your whimsical little world again?

items.speaker: Ritualist
items.text: In case such practical matters slipped your mind, your witless rabble were supposed to be hunting down the Foundation's arcanists.

items.speaker: Ustrina
items.text: All is in hand. Though there has been some unexpected reluctance from them. The reason for which still eludes me.

items.speaker: Ritualist
items.text: You're trying to understand them?
Her staff slams against the gray and white checkered floor.

items.speaker: Ritualist
items.text: I can't waste any more breath on this.
She passes Ustrina and leaves through the building's other exit.
Stomping feet echo through the corridor, fortunately concealing another's approach.
Southern Annex, St. Pavlov Foundation
The ritualist arrives at an outdoor space behind the building, where the wide-open gardens are replaced with tidy pathways.

items.speaker: Ritualist
items.text: With those Flying Witches focused on the gardens and the plaza, this location must suffice.
Prima.
She whips her head around to face the voice's source.

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: I didn't expect to find you working alone. You've grown careless.

items.speaker: Ritualist
items.text: Grace? Impossible. How did you get here?

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: As I always do. You of all people should know my means.

items.speaker: Ritualist
items.text: *sneer* And you think you can simply show your face here and get away unscathed?

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: Come on, then. Let's see what tricks you've picked up in my absence.

items.speaker: Ritualist
items.text: *choke*

items.speaker: Ritualist
items.text: Grace, you deceitful parasite! I'll make you pay for my mother's death in Antarctica.

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: Level your accusations later. Now, tell me how you got past the Foundation's security.

items.speaker: Ritualist
items.text: *cough* Traitor, thief! You'll get nothing from me.

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: Enough, Prima. I don't have time for your tantrums.

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: Stay calm. This will only take a moment. You might even survive if you're lucky.

items.speaker: Ritualist
items.text: I curse you, Grace! You'll never be free. You'll die a pathetic, sniveling slave.
The moth beats its wings once more and flutters away from Ms. Stranger's fingertip, then lands on the ritualist's face.

items.speaker: Ritualist
items.text: Take it off. Get this thing off my face!
It's as if something sucks away the air around them.
Then the moth forged by her arcane skill turns into fine powder before their eyes.

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: No. What? What's happening?

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: Don't stay out in the open like that, Nautika. You're too exposed.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: It's okay. They can't hurt me, really.

items.speaker: Manus Soldier I
items.text: Damn it!
The Manus's attacks on Nautika glance off her like water over a stone.
Ricocheting incantations slam against the walls. Fortunately, the Committee Building is sturdy enough to withstand them.

items.speaker: Foundation Security
items.text: Take this: Smashing Bouncing Ball!
A fist-sized sphere flies out from behind cover, bouncing off the floor, walls, and ceiling.

items.speaker: Manus Soldier I
items.text: Get down! Ugh!
The ball smashes a dent into a black helmet.

items.speaker: Foundation Security
items.text: You've got to give them credit. Those Laplace brainiacs sure know how to build some solid toys.

items.speaker: Soldier I
items.text: Impressive. But I still don't get why you have to shout that bloody name every time.

items.speaker: Foundation Security
items.text: The higher the volume, the greater the damage. That's what the guy in the tin box said.

items.speaker: Soldier I
items.text: Alright, can't hurt to have a little fun. Let me try one.
The security staff and soldiers fall back behind cover and continue making use of their new "toys."
Meanwhile, from the other end of the battleground, Krutov observes the escalating counterattack.

items.speaker: Krutov
items.text: Their Chimera is immune to our incantations. Nothing a swift bullet to the head couldn't solve, if that druid weren't so incessant.

items.speaker: Krutov
items.text: We don't have the forces for close-quarters combat. Where the hell is our heavy firepower?
He steps back a bit, attempting to get a wider field of view. His troops are on the edge of breaking. The unthinkable occurs: A tactical retreat may be necessary.
But then, Arcana appears.
An indescribable force compels Krutov to step aside.
The battle of black and white comes to an eerie pause. All present seem to be paralyzed with awe and terror.

items.speaker: Arcana
items.text: It is a wondrous form thou hast claimed, Nautika. I cannot help but behold thy beauty with some awe.

items.speaker: Arcana
items.text: Did we not return to this world upon the same blessed day? Pray tell—how fares thy second life, and the powers thou hast seized?

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: My-My life has nothing to do with you, Arcana.
Arcana's focus shifts, not dismissively, but as effortless as a turning wind.

items.speaker: Arcana
items.text: Ms. Weyerhaeuser? Charming as ever. What a delight to chance upon thee here as well.

items.speaker: Arcana
items.text: Too long has it been e'er last we spoke. And a question hath weighed upon me since then: why protect these humans, the cause of thy family's ruin?
She takes a step closer.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: Leave her to me!
Nautika spreads her wings and lunges at Arcana.
Yet Arcana stands unmoved and unafraid, as if she is only watching a performance.

items.speaker: Arcana
items.text: Hush, child.
Druvis's thorns wither away, and Nautika comes crashing to the marble floor below.
Her entire body feels heavy, as if she had been drained of all strength. With effort, she manages to move her upper half, but her lower limbs are motionless.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: I ... I can't get up.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: Something's wrong.
Each and every arcanist feels it, a sensation like having the air ripped from their lungs, like being pulled down to the ocean floor, at once both pressure and suffocation.
The massive tree behind them begins to buckle and shake until it comes crashing down.

items.speaker: Druvis III
items.text: There are still people under the tree.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: No. My adventure ...
Arcanists across the battlefield begin to waver and collapse into unconsciousness.
Arcana stands at the other end of the long hall, wearing a satisfied expression, like an artist overlooking their work.

items.speaker: Arcana
items.text: Rise.
She is suddenly pulled up into the air as if weightless.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: Something's picking me up.

items.speaker: Arcana
items.text: Fall.
She sinks back down only to be pulled to one side, her body dragging against the rubble-strewn floor.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: N-No! I can't stop!
Then, with a flick of her wrist, Arcana sends Nautika and all the people, objects, and foliage in her path hurtling out of the building.

items.speaker: Arcana
items.text: At last, some peace and quiet.
